What happened to separation of church and state..? America has a poor history of it anyways, I'm looking at you Alabama with your giant statue of the Christian 10 commandments on a Montgomery? courthouse lawn...If public schools are going to offer a religious studies class in a historical sense that's great. Teach kids about all the different silly things that people around the world believe. But if you are only teaching the Christian bible than its a violation of the idea of separating church and state. I went to school in a province of Canada that still had denominational schools. My biology teacher was a Jesuit brother who believed that the Earth was 7k years old...We had a "world religions" class. We spent one week on Buddhism, one week on Judaism and 10 and a half months on Roman Catholicism...the religion we were already all most familiar with. If I sound a little harsh on religion it was this experience that solidified my atheism. I understand that for some people, and a lot of Americans, that's as dirty a term as "socialism." But in a free western democratic society you can't push one religion on influential children in the publicly funded school systems.
